Container.Name: Stackyard
Container.Overview: A self-hosted homelab dashboard you actually want to look at.[br][br]Most dashboards are a wall of numbers and charts. Stackyard is the opposite: a calm, launcher-style grid of app tiles, folders, and a small number of genuinely useful widgets. Built to be glanced at a hundred times a day without feeling cluttered.[br][br]Everything is set up from the browser. Add app tiles, group them into folders, arrange pages, and drop in widgets for the services you already run. Widgets cover Docker, system health, downloads, media, backups, network and more.[br][br]Runs as one container with no external database and no runtime dependencies. Configuration and uploaded icons persist in the two paths below.[br][br]Note: most homelab services live on private addresses. The Allow Private IPs setting below is on by default so links and widgets pointing at your other containers work. Turn it off to keep the SSRF guard enabled.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: homelab dashboard homepage self-hosted launcher start page widgets
Container.DonateText: If Stackyard is useful to you, you can buy me a coffee.
Container.Changes:
### 1.22.0 - 2026-11-10
### Added
- Print a one-time setup code to the container log when an address is refused, so a password can be set on that address.
- Add `INITIAL_PASSWORD` and `INITIAL_PASSWORD_FILE` to set the dashboard password on the first start.
- Add a Confirm Password field and a show-password button to the Settings password.
- Add a Reorder mode with Move Up and Move Down buttons to the Dashboard list.
- Add a popover to every badge that names its source and shows when it may be out of date.
- Add a VoiceOver page control to the phone dashboard.
- Animate the Settings navigation icons and the Add New type tiles on hover.
### Changed
- Require at least 15 characters for a new password and refuse common passwords. Existing passwords keep working.
- Show a character count toward the minimum instead of a strength score while a password is typed.
- Sign out all devices now signs out this browser as well.
- Confirm saves on the Save button and report deletes as Deleted.
- Write error messages as instructions and dialog titles as questions.
- Show the sign-in lockout wait in minutes.
- Keep widgets on a theme change and crossfade instead of reloading them.
- Roll changed digits in System Summary, DNS and Weather.
- Fade in the wallpaper and badges.
- Show the "Stackyard isn't responding" screen in the last used language.
- Keep catalogue icons in the browser for a day, so repeat visits make fewer requests.
- Request Unsplash wallpapers at the size of the screen and in a modern format.
- Start loading the wallpaper first and show its colour straight away.
- Restore the dashboard instantly with Back, after checking sign-in and settings.
- Show the Settings form only once its real values have loaded.
- `TRUSTED_PROXY` accepts the proxy's container name, and warns when an entry covers a whole network.
- Audit lines for password and protection changes record the client address and host.
- Importing a backup from a newer Stackyard version is now refused.
- Widget animations use less CPU and pause off screen.
- Remove the bounce from dashboard tile presses.
- Dragging near a screen edge scrolls faster the closer the pointer is to the edge.
- Redraw the interface icons in one consistent style.
- Disk Health shows the friendly name set in Scrutiny.
- Dashboard buttons and page dots respond when pressed.
- System Summary figures animate only on larger changes.
- Settings sections no longer slide when switching.
### Fixed
- Let the owner set a new password with a setup code when the saved password is damaged, instead of being locked out.
- Accept a password with accents whether the device types them composed or decomposed.
- Let password managers save and fill the dashboard password, filed under the host name.
- Keep focus on the folder Add button after adding an app to a folder.
- Show Weather in light colours after a live switch to light mode.
- Fill the screen on a sideways phone when no tall widget needs the extra rows.
- Keep the photo credit clear of widgets on a sideways phone.
- Keep each stored value when two secret badge rows share a name.
- Saving Settings no longer reverts a change made on another device.
- An imported file with invalid values no longer freezes the dashboard or stops Settings from loading.
- An item with the id `settings` no longer blocks every later save.
- Saving a very large dashboard no longer stalls the server.
- Failed saves now say why: full disk, no write access, a file mounted on its own, or a config over the size limit.
- Turning protection off no longer deletes a password that was changed while the old one was being checked.
- A sign-in refused as busy no longer uses up an attempt.
- Settings says when protection was turned off but other settings were not saved.
- A backup from an early version with non-app items in a folder can be restored.
- Dashboard Switch keys no longer stay raised after a tap on a touch screen.
- Numbers in Clock, DNS and Weather no longer shift sideways as they change.
- Backup job times stay current between refreshes.
- Now Playing shows right-to-left titles in the correct direction.
- Show badges without animating them when the dashboard loads.
- Scrolling search results on a phone no longer opens a result.
- Folder page dots work with assistive technology, and arrow keys turn folder pages.
- The empty search message is readable in the light theme.
- Long values in Settings drop-downs no longer collapse or shift the row.
- Dragging a row on a phone scrolls above the tab bar.
- Small Settings controls have larger touch areas.
- Settings scrolling respects the reduced motion preference.
- The phone search button no longer changes shape when the page loads.
- Keyboard focus stays visible on bright wallpapers and no longer changes a control's shape.
- Page dots stay distinguishable with Increase Contrast.
- Reduce Transparency now gives solid dashboard surfaces.
- Long badge labels stay inside the badge.
- Persian search results show addresses and arrows in the right direction.
- A config change no longer reloads the dashboard during search, a folder or a drag.
- Long names and translated text stay inside widgets.
- Screen readers no longer repeat Now Playing on every refresh.
- Disk Health works with a mouse on touch-capable devices.
- Backup status is shown in words on the card back.
- Widgets follow Increase Contrast.
- Dashboard Switch shows an error when its settings fail to load.
- Keyboard focus is visible on the row being edited and on the selected colour.
- Save and other long actions show that they are working and ignore a second press.
- Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast now apply to Settings surfaces.
- Dialogs and controls fit on the smallest phones.
- Searching a long app list no longer stutters.
- Screen readers announce how many items match a search.
- An app with the id `settings` no longer blocks every Settings save.
- A folder whose app list is malformed no longer stops the dashboard and Settings from loading.
- Deleting from an editor removes that item, even after a backup restore or an import changed the list.
- A slow save no longer closes an editor opened while it ran.
- Keyboard focus opens a badge's popover again after the dashboard redraws.
- Show the password strength meter again when the password is edited a second time.
### Security
- Refuse sign-in and password requests larger than 32 KB, so parallel large requests to these routes can no longer exhaust the container's memory.
- Refuse a sign-in checked against a password that was changed meanwhile.
- Count failed sign-ins from one IPv6 /64 against a single limit.
- Hide a newly typed password in Settings instead of showing it in the row.
- Never send a stored widget secret to a row whose address changed when two rows share an id.
- Accept only a GitHub login name as the GitHub widget username.
- Use a changed Proxmox secret at once instead of a result fetched with the old one.
- Keep text of a damaged config file out of the log.
- Refuse cloud metadata addresses on every outbound request, even with `ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS=true`.
- Allow a container name to reach only containers on a shared Docker network when `ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS` is off.
- Apply the Host IP exception only when the setting holds an IP address.
- Require the setup code from the container log to set the first password.
- Refuse requests that came through a proxy on an unlisted address while no password is set.
- Check one password at a time, so parallel sign-ins at a large `PASSWORD_HASH_MEMORY` no longer exhaust the container's memory.
- Cap sign-in log lines so a flood of refused attempts cannot push earlier entries out of the log.
- Mark the session cookie `Secure` when the page was loaded over https.
- Keep the `Secure` flag on the session cookie when a renewal request does not show the page scheme.
- Run the Compose example with a read-only root filesystem.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port the dashboard is reached on.

Config.Name: Config Storage
Config.Description: Dashboard configuration. Keep this, or every setting is lost on update.

Config.Name: Icon Storage
Config.Description: Icons you upload for your app tiles.

Config.Name: Allow Private IPs
Config.Description: Let widgets and badges reach private addresses, which most homelab services use. Set to false to keep the SSRF guard on.

Config.Name: Docker Socket Proxy URL
Config.Description: Optional. Address of a Docker socket proxy, for the Docker widgets. Example: http://socket-proxy:2375

Config.Name: Trust Proxy
Config.Description: Optional. Set to true behind a reverse proxy that terminates HTTPS, so the sign-in cookie is marked HTTPS-only.

Config.Name: Node Options
Config.Description: Node heap cap. Keep it near half the --memory limit in Extra Parameters, and raise both together.
